judge: one LLM-assisted reviewer (Claude), not independent domain experts; judged from problem statement, status rationale, work title and OpenAlex abstract

definitions.correct: the paper does what the verdict says to a claim or question in the problem statement
definitions.partly: the paper bears on the problem but advances, solves a sub-case, or contradicts an adjacent or rival claim
definitions.wrong: the paper does not do what the verdict says

patterns.methods_fail: current methods fail, read as refuting an open 'can it be done' problem
patterns.rival: refutes a rival explanation or prior result, not the problem
patterns.answers: answers or advances a sub-question, labelled refutes
patterns.adjacent: evidence from an adjacent or restricted setting
patterns.source: source paper of the phenomenon labelled refutes

items.work_title: Efficient Sequence Packing without Cross-contamination: Accelerating Large Language Models without Impacting Performance
items.llm_quote: Formulates sequence packing as a bin packing problem and gives algorithms that remove padding waste in LLM pre-training without cross-contamination in attention.
items.reason: Packing with a block-diagonal mask removes contamination at BERT scale; the effect of contamination on LLM pretraining is not measured.

items.work_title: Privacy of Noisy Stochastic Gradient Descent: More Iterations Without More Privacy Loss
items.llm_quote: Gives a tight characterization of the differential privacy of noisy SGD (Langevin dynamics) for smooth convex losses over a bounded domain. It shows that privacy loss stops growing after a burn-in period.
items.reason: Tight privacy bound for noisy SGD, but only for smooth convex losses on a bounded domain; the nonconvex case in the title stays open.

items.work_title: It's Not a Modality Gap: Characterizing and Addressing the Contrastive Gap
items.llm_quote: Adding uniformity and alignment terms to the CLIP loss closes the gap and improves downstream performance.
items.reason: Gives one explanation (the contrastive loss creates the gap) and a loss fix; a single self-claim among competing explanations.

items.work_title: Two Counterexamples to Tokenization and the Noiseless Channel
items.llm_quote: Two BPE tokenization variants can arbitrarily increase Rényi efficiency while decreasing downstream model performance.
items.reason: Counterexamples break one intrinsic metric (Renyi efficiency); the question whether any intrinsic statistic predicts outcomes stays open.

items.work_title: Learning to Deceive with Attention-Based Explanations
items.llm_quote: Models reduce attention on impermissible tokens while still relying on them, with little accuracy cost across models and tasks.
items.reason: Models can put low attention on tokens they still rely on, so attention weight need not track causal contribution.

items.work_title: Do pretrained Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent?
items.llm_quote: in LLaMa-7B ICL and GD differ in order sensitivity and in how they modify the output distribution.
items.reason: Statement names the claim; on LLaMa-7B, ICL and GD differ in order sensitivity and output shift. Empirical, pretrained LLMs only.

items.work_title: Noise Is Not the Main Factor Behind the Gap Between SGD and Adam on Transformers, but Sign Descent Might Be
items.llm_quote: Stochasticity and heavy-tailed noise are not major factors in the SGD-Adam performance gap.
items.reason: Refutes one candidate explanation (heavy-tailed noise) of the Adam-SGD gap; the gap itself is confirmed.

items.work_title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Behavior Steering Interventions in LLMs
items.llm_quote: Some interventions are less effective than previously reported.
items.reason: Proposes an evaluation protocol; 'some interventions less effective than reported' is weak counter-evidence.

items.work_title: Analyzing the Generalization and Reliability of Steering Vectors
items.llm_quote: In-distribution, steerability is highly variable across inputs, and spurious biases can substantially affect steering effectiveness depending on the concept.
items.reason: Statement claims steering is reliable and generalises; paper finds high per-input variance and weak OOD generalisation.

items.work_title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
items.llm_quote: For steering, prompting outperforms all existing methods, followed by finetuning.
items.reason: Statement claims steering beats prompting as a control surface; AxBench finds prompting beats all steering methods (Gemma-2 2B/9B).

items.work_title: The shutdown problem: an AI engineering puzzle for decision theorists
items.llm_quote: Proves three theorems showing that agents meeting seemingly innocuous conditions will often try to prevent or cause the press, even at a cost.
items.reason: Theorems show agents meeting stated conditions resist or cause shutdown; an impossibility under assumptions, which the author says guides solutions.

items.work_title: Single-Turn Debate Does Not Help Humans Answer Hard Reading-Comprehension Questions
items.llm_quote: Explanations did not improve human accuracy.
items.reason: Single-turn, non-interactive arguments did not help humans; multi-turn debate with a judge is not tested.

items.work_title: If Influence Functions Are the Answer, Then What is the Question?
items.llm_quote: Influence estimates are often a good approximation to the PBRF even when poor for leave-one-out retraining.
items.reason: Influence estimates track the PBRF, not leave-one-out retraining; this answers the 'what do they estimate' sub-question rather than refuting it. No scale or stability result.

items.work_title: On the Limitations of Unsupervised Bilingual Dictionary Induction
items.llm_quote: Induction performs much worse on morphologically rich languages that are not dependent marking, and under domain or embedding-algorithm mismatch.
items.reason: Unsupervised dictionary induction fails on some languages and under domain mismatch; shows limits of current methods, not impossibility.

items.work_title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
items.llm_quote: The incompatibility view is one-sided and imperfect; there are circumstances where label smoothing does lose effectiveness.
items.reason: Argues the LS-KD incompatibility view is one-sided but also confirms it holds in some cases; characterises 'when', which is the problem's ask.

items.work_title: Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt
items.llm_quote: The reported estimates fail to fit the extracted data and are inconsistent with the first two methods.
items.reason: Refutes Hoffmann et al.'s third-method fit, but the rederived law agrees with methods 1-2 (about 20 tokens/parameter).

items.work_title: On the Impact of Calibration Data in Post-training Quantization and Pruning
items.llm_quote: Substantial variations in downstream task performance depending on calibration data, contrary to prior claims of robustness.
items.reason: Shows calibration data changes downstream accuracy, contradicting prior robustness claims; this answers the empirical question rather than refuting it.

items.work_title: Pruning Neural Networks at Initialization: Why are We Missing the Mark?
items.llm_quote: These methods beat random pruning but fall short of magnitude pruning after training.
items.reason: Current pruning-at-init methods fall short of post-training pruning; not a proof that tickets cannot be found at initialisation.

items.work_title: NF4 Isn't Information Theoretically Optimal (and that's Good)
items.llm_quote: argues NF4 is not information-theoretically optimal because the distribution of values to quantize depends on block size.
items.reason: Shows NF4 is not information-theoretically optimal (value distribution depends on block size); contradicts a specific optimality claim.

items.work_title: Compressing LLMs: The Truth is Rarely Pure and Never Simple
items.llm_quote: Introduces LLM-KICK, a knowledge-intensive benchmark for evaluating compressed LLMs, arguing that perplexity misses capability changes. Pruning degrades sharply, even at 25-30% sparsity
items.reason: Statement names the implicit sufficiency claim; LLM-KICK shows matched perplexity with sharp knowledge-task loss (e.g. 25-30% sparsity).

items.work_title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics are not Robust
items.llm_quote: Circuit faithfulness scores reflect researchers' methodological choices as well as the circuit's components; the task a circuit performs depends on the ablation used.
items.reason: Existing circuit faithfulness scores depend on ablation choices; negative result on current metrics, not on the problem.

items.work_title: Planting Undetectable Backdoors in Machine Learning Models
items.llm_quote: The constructions imply a barrier to certifying adversarial robustness.
items.reason: Undetectable backdoors are a barrier to certifying a model supplied by an untrusted trainer; does not bound smoothing radii for honest training.

items.work_title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
items.llm_quote: 100% attack success rate by GPT-4 judge on many models including Llama-3-Instruct-8B, GPT-4o and R2D2.
items.reason: 100% ASR on many aligned models shows current defences break; does not show robustness or certification impossible.

items.work_title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
items.llm_quote: 89% ASR on GPT-4o with 10,000 augmented prompts.
items.reason: High attack success on deployed models shows current defences break; does not show robustness or certification impossible.

items.work_title: An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
items.llm_quote: Finetuning on 10 unrelated examples or removing specific activation directions recovers most hazardous capabilities of RMU-edited models.
items.reason: Recovers capabilities from RMU-unlearned models; refutes one method's claim, not the possibility of provable unlearning.

items.work_title: A Closer Look at Accuracy vs. Robustness
items.llm_quote: Argues that real image datasets are separated and that locally Lipschitz functions can achieve both robustness and accuracy, so no inherent tradeoff exists.
items.reason: Argues the tradeoff is an artifact on separated datasets; takes one side of the theory variant, which is an advance, not a refutation.

items.work_title: Students Parrot Their Teachers: Membership Inference on Model Distillation
items.llm_quote: Finds distillation alone gives limited privacy, and attacks can succeed even when the target is never queried on actual training points.
items.reason: Statement names the folk claim that students are safer; membership inference shows distillation gives limited privacy.

items.work_title: Exposure Bias versus Self-Recovery: Are Distortions Really Incremental for Autoregressive Text Generation?
items.llm_quote: Distortion from prefix discrepancy is limited and not incremental during generation; LMs show self-recovery.
items.reason: Exposure bias is limited in open-ended LM generation; no distillation experiment.

items.work_title: Counterfactually-Augmented SNLI Training Data Does Not Yield Better Generalization Than Unaugmented Data
items.llm_quote: Models trained on counterfactually-augmented SNLI do not generalize better than unaugmented data of similar size, and augmentation can hurt robustness to challenge examples.
items.reason: Counterfactual augmentation did not improve generalisation over size-matched data on SNLI; one task.

items.work_title: Pitfalls of Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification through Loss Minimisation
items.llm_quote: It shows that the proposed loss functions do not incentivise a faithful representation of epistemic uncertainty.
items.reason: Second-order loss minimisation does not represent epistemic uncertainty faithfully; negative result for one method class.

items.work_title: Benchmarking Uncertainty Disentanglement: Specialized Uncertainties for Specialized Tasks
items.llm_quote: No existing approach yields truly disentangled estimator pairs in practice, and specialized tasks are harder than predictive uncertainty tasks.
items.reason: Benchmark finds no estimator disentangles in practice (ImageNet); does not show the split unidentifiable.

items.work_title: How Good is the Bayes Posterior in Deep Neural Networks Really?
items.llm_quote: Bayes posterior predictions are systematically worse than SGD point estimates; a cold posterior improves performance significantly.
items.reason: This is Wenzel et al. 2020, the paper that reports the cold posterior effect; it supports the statement.

items.work_title: What Are Bayesian Neural Network Posteriors Really Like?
items.llm_quote: Posterior tempering is not needed for near-optimal performance; the cold posterior effect is largely an artifact of data augmentation.
items.reason: Full-batch HMC: tempering not needed, effect largely from data augmentation; an explanation that contradicts Wenzel et al., itself contested.

items.work_title: Data augmentation in Bayesian neural networks and the cold posterior effect
items.llm_quote: The cold posterior effect persists in principled models with data augmentation.
items.reason: Effect persists with principled augmentation; refutes the augmentation explanation, and supports the phenomenon.

items.work_title: Deep Ensembles Work, but Are They Necessary?
items.llm_quote: Shows that the uncertainty and robustness benefits of deep ensembles can be replicated by a single larger network.
items.reason: A larger single network matches ensemble uncertainty and robustness; challenges a premise, does not say what ensembles do.

items.work_title: The complexity of homomorphism and constraint satisfaction problems seen from the other side
items.llm_quote: HOM(C,−) is in polynomial time iff C has bounded treewidth modulo homomorphic equivalence, under a parameterized complexity assumption.
items.reason: Grohe 2007 closes the bounded-arity case (treewidth modulo homomorphic equivalence, under an FPT assumption); unbounded arity and counting/enumeration stay open.

items.work_title: Tractable Hypergraph Properties for Constraint Satisfaction and Conjunctive Queries
items.llm_quote: Unbounded submodular width implies CSP(H) is not FPT unless ETH fails.
items.reason: Marx 2013 gives the FPT frontier (submodular width, under ETH) for unbounded arity; polynomial-time frontier and #CQ stay open.

items.work_title: Expressiveness and complexity of order dependencies
items.llm_quote: Inference for UODs (and ODs) is coNP-complete.
items.reason: Settles coNP-completeness of list-based OD inference; approximate, bidirectional and set-based variants and optimizer use are untouched.

items.work_title: The Hunt for a Red Spider: Conjunctive Query Determinacy Is Undecidable
items.llm_quote: Shows that unrestricted conjunctive query determinacy is undecidable.
items.reason: Shows unrestricted CQ determinacy undecidable, which the statement names as the central open problem; rewriting and finite variants are separate.

items.work_title: Crowdsourcing algorithms for entity resolution
items.llm_quote: Shows a previously claimed optimal strategy can be arbitrarily bad and proposes strategies with guarantees
items.reason: Shows a prior strategy (Wang et al.) can be arbitrarily bad and gives strategies with guarantees; contradicts a prior result, not the problem.

items.work_title: Two-sided RDMA Striking Back for Disaggregated Memory Databases
items.llm_quote: Lotus achieves up to 8.2x higher throughput than state-of-the-art one-sided RDMA approaches on YCSB.
items.reason: Lotus reports two-sided RDMA throughput over one-sided systems; it does not show correct one-sided indexes impossible.
